title: Cap. 3 Obj. 16: Application already firm in the death itself — so not applicable where not applied
pass_a_gloss: Obj.16: absurd death applicable where not applied — firmest application already in the death for all for whom truly died → only elect-known-to-God. Sol: deny absurdity. Nude offering obtains: all who will believe are saved — Gospel promises that world-wide; named infallible application not preachable. Death ordained to all to whom remission-by-faith-in-blood can be announced (any human-nature participant); infallible application to elect alone because certainty hangs on eternal predestinating act, not on offering alone. Dual intention: general (liberate any who believe) + special (give faith/salvation to sheep per election). What special predestination gives some must not overturn what offering acquires for all.
pass_b_english: Obj. 16. It is absurd to posit that Christ’s death by Divine ordination is a lytron applicable to those to whom it is not applied; because in Christ’s death itself there was the firmest application of the death for all those for whom he is truly affirmed to have died and suffered: Therefore Christ’s death is not a remedy ordained by God except for certain singular elect persons known to God alone, to whom at length as to the event it is saving.

Sol. We deny that anything absurd inheres in the aforesaid opinion, which we have demonstrated to be true and agreeable to Divine wisdom. But what is objected — That as regards all for whom Christ died, an infallible application of the death is also included in that same death of Christ — does not seem to us to be conceded. For Christ’s offering considered in itself nakedly obtains and gets from God this universally, that all and each who have been willing to believe in Christ are saved. The Gospel preaches and promises this efficacy of Christ’s death to the whole world: but that infallible purpose of applying this death to these or those persons evangelical heralds cannot promise by name to any mortal. We say that Christ’s death is ordained for all those to whom remission of sins through faith in his blood can be announced: which grace looks to any participant of human nature. But we confess that Christ’s death is to be applied infallibly to the elect alone; because the certainty of application depends, as from a primary cause, on the secret and eternal act of God predestinating, not on the sole fact of Christ offering himself for human beings. Christ therefore in offering himself had a general intention conforming to the Father’s ordination, namely that he might indiscriminately free any human beings whatever, provided they believed in him, from the guilt of sins, and in this sense he is said to have offered himself for all. He also had, as conscious of Divine predestination, a special intention conforming to the Father’s secret and eternal good-pleasure, namely that for the sheep to be given to him according to the decree of election he might from the merit of his death obtain and give faith, salvation, all things: and with this special intention he is said to have laid down his life for his peculiar people, that is, for certain singular persons. What comes to certain ones from Christ’s death through a special act of Divine predestination ought not to overturn what was acquired for all through the very act of offering. Let infallible application rather be ascribed to predestination; but that Christ’s death is applicable to all and each through faith, let it be assigned to the offering itself from the tenor of the Divine covenant.
